question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (Cat III AIF) is reviewing its investor-count compliance. What is the SEBI cap on number of investors per scheme of an AIF?

answer.text: No more than 200 investors per scheme, without exception
No more than 1,000 investors per scheme; Accredited Investors are EXCLUDED from the count
No more than 100 investors per scheme, without exception
No more than 1,000 investors per scheme including all AIs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Third Amendment) Regulations 2025, no scheme of an AIF shall have more than 1,000 investors. Accredited Investors are EXCLUDED while computing this number. In a company-form AIF, the Companies Act 2013 limits private-placement investors to 200. The Trap: Option A (200) is Companies-Act cap, not SEBI AIF cap. Option C (100) is a wrong figure. Option D fails to exclude AIs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test the same cap. XIX-E cares because AI-only and LVF schemes are unlimited. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your scheme is nearing the cap, push marketing toward AI-segment investors — they don't count against the 1,000. Monitor onboarding dashboard monthly.
